label: Typika (Obednitsa)
description: The Reader's Office of the Typika (Obednitsa). Celebrated in the absence of a priest or Divine Liturgy on Sundays and feasts, in place of Holy Communion. Consists of Psalms 102 and 145 with the "O Only-begotten Son" hymn, the Beatitudes, the Heavenly Choir hymn, the Symbol of Faith, "Loose, remit, pardon," the Lord's Prayer, the day's Kontakion, and appointed Epistle and Gospel readings.

sections.label: Opening
sections.notes: The Typika opens with the Usual Beginning, as do all Byzantine offices.

items.text:
The Priest blesses: Blessed is our God, always, now and ever and unto ages of ages.
If no Priest is present, the Reader begins: Through the prayers of our holy fathers, Lord Jesus Christ our God, have mercy on us and save us. Amen.

items.label: The Usual Beginning
items.note: Trisagion prayers sequence. Resolved from typika-fixed.json by HorologionEngine.

sections.label: Psalms 102 and 145
sections.notes: Two psalms appointed at the Typika: Psalm 102 (LXX) -- Bless the Lord, O my soul; and Psalm 145 (LXX) -- Praise the Lord, O my soul; followed by the fixed hymn "O Only-begotten Son, and Word of God." Both sources place this psalmody BEFORE the Beatitudes, not after (Finding T2).

items.label: Psalm 102 (LXX) — Bless the Lord, O my soul
Psalm 145 (LXX) — Praise the Lord, O my soul
O Only-Begotten Son, and Word of God

sections.label: The Beatitudes
sections.notes: The Beatitudes (Matthew 5:3–12) with refrains. Appointed at the Typika in place of the Antiphons of the Liturgy.

items.label: The Beatitudes (Matthew 5:3–12)
items.note: Fixed text, including its own closing refrain ("Remember us, O Lord/Master/Holy One"). Resolved from typika-fixed.json by HorologionEngine.

sections.label: The Heavenly Choir
sections.notes: Between the Beatitudes' closing refrain and the Creed, both sources give this three-part hymn (Finding T4).

items.label: The Heavenly Choir Doth Hymn Thee

sections.label: Symbol of Faith
sections.notes: The Nicene-Constantinopolitan Creed, followed directly by the fixed prayer "Loose, remit, pardon, O God, our transgressions" (Finding T6) -- both sources place it here, immediately after the Creed and before the Lord's Prayer.

items.label: Loose, Remit, Pardon, O God, Our Transgressions

sections.label: The Lord's Prayer
sections.notes: The Lord's Prayer, said once, directly after the Creed and "Loose, remit, pardon" -- both sources place it here, immediately before the day's Kontakion (Findings T5, T6). (Previously duplicated: once here, correctly, and once inside the now-removed spurious Trisagion block.)

items.label: Kontakion of the Day
items.note: Sunday: the Resurrectional Kontakion by tone (already fixed, unchanged by this audit fix). Monday-Saturday: a fixed day-of-week table (Finding T7 -- HAPGOOD1922 pp.61-62), resolved by HorologionEngine. A feast or commemorated saint from the Menaion, when present, takes precedence over this fixed table; that override is not built (same deferred-pending-Menaion-import status as troparion-of-the-day).

sections.label: Epistle and Gospel
sections.notes: The appointed Epistle and Gospel for the day are read. Appointments follow the Apostol and Evangelist.

items.text: EPISTLE: The appointed Epistle reading for the day from the Apostol is read here. Consult the Apostol for the appointed pericope according to the day and tone.
GOSPEL: The appointed Gospel reading for the day from the Evangelist is read here. Consult the Evangelist for the appointed pericope according to the day and tone.

sections.label: Dismissal
sections.notes: A structural dismissal rubric closes the office.

items.text:
Lord, have mercy. (×3)
Glory to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit, both now and ever, and unto ages of ages. Amen.

If a Priest is present: the Priest gives the dismissal according to the day and feast.
If no Priest is present: Through the prayers of our holy fathers, Lord Jesus Christ our God, have mercy on us and save us. Amen.
